title: 4Sum II
statement: You are given four integer arrays `a`, `b`, `c`, and `d`. Return the number of tuples (i, j, k, l) such that a[i] + b[j] + c[k] + d[l] == 0.
hints: Four nested loops count tuples correctly and are too slow at n = 200.
Split the sum into (a + b) and (c + d). The second pair must be the negation of the first.
Store every a+b sum in a frequency map, then probe -(c+d).

approaches.name: Meet in the middle
approaches.explanation: Hash one pair of arrays and probe the other pair.

editorial: Every tuple splits into two pairs. Compute all n squared sums from the first two arrays and count them. Each sum from the last two arrays looks up the negation. Multiplying is unnecessary: the map already stores how many ways the complement can be formed, so you add that count.
